research_period: Milan, Paris and Pitti Uomo menswear shows, June 2026; Premiere Vision Paris, February 2026; analysis July to November 2026
markets: Global: Milan, Paris and Florence runways; premium and mid-market menswear
title: SS27 Men's Ventilated Tailoring
summary: The suit adapts to heat: lighter, open-necked and in places transparent, in silk, gauze, seersucker and perforated leather.

sections.heading: The story
sections.body: Milan designers "went lighter" in silhouette and broadly agreed that a well-dressed man still wears a suit, but the suit is adapting<sup>[1]</sup>: lighter, less oversized tailoring with open necklines and more airflow, dress shirts left unbuttoned or rendered transparent<sup>[1]</sup>. Thom Browne showed layered seersucker suiting<sup>[1]</sup>. In Paris, Jonathan Anderson's Dior collection had fluid suits in very light, almost sheer silk and gauze<sup>[2]</sup>, and Hypebeast tracked sheer double-breasted suits at Dior and sheer trousers at Hed Mayner<sup>[3]</sup>. At Pitti Uomo, Herno launched crease-proof travel pieces in stretch wool and technical fabrics<sup>[4]</sup>.

sections.heading: Colours
sections.body: Ice blue, sand and white, with tobacco for depth. See SS27 Men's Season Colours.

sections.heading: Silhouettes
sections.body:
- Unlined, soft-shoulder jackets with open-necked shirts.
- Lighter double-breasted suits.
- Long trousers cut closer to the body.

sections.heading: Fabrics
sections.body: Silk and gauze<sup>[2]</sup>, seersucker<sup>[1]</sup>, perforated and woven leather<sup>[1]</sup>, fine lightweight wools blended with silk or linen<sup>[5]</sup>, crease-proof stretch wool<sup>[4]</sup>.

sections.heading: Trims and details
sections.body: Minimal canvas and interlining, unlined backs, mother-of-pearl buttons, open-weave and perforated panels.

timing: In stores February to July 2027; strongest for wedding season and summer events. Forecut expects lighter tailoring to carry into SS28.
products:
- Unlined summer suits; seersucker suits; linen travel suits; sheer or semi-sheer shirts.
- Customers: working men who still wear tailoring in hot climates; wedding guests.
design_implications:
- Remove weight: half-canvas or unconstructed fronts, quarter lining.
- Test semi-sheer shirting for modesty and comfort before committing.
- Use crease-recovery and stretch wool for travel pieces.
commercial_implications:
- Lead tailoring with summer weights rather than four-season cloth.
- Price sheer and silk pieces at premium; seersucker and linen at mid.
